summary.text: 学 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學 and is used for learning and study. Its visible graph has an upper assembly above 子; that modern split does not settle the disputed construction of 學.

formation.text: The current graph 学 is arranged ⿳⺍冖子: ⺍ and 冖 together form an upper assembly above 子. This visible split does not settle how traditional 學 was first constructed. One account interprets oracle-bone forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Separate proposals describe associative forms involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖; phonosemantic forms with 爻 as sound and 升 or 冖 as the other element; a rare element read jù, described as hands or claws and assigned both sound and meaning roles; and a distinct construction involving two 臼 forms with 冖. Another proposal says 子 was added in Western Zhou forms to mark a child learner. These are competing interpretations, not a settled reconstruction. The modern simplified shape does not establish the ancient structure.

components.text: This is the visible top part of the upper assembly in 学’s ⿳⺍冖子 arrangement. No historical, semantic, or phonetic function is established for it.
冖 is the visible middle component below ⺍ and above 子 in 学. Its identity here does not establish a roof meaning or an ancient role.
子 is visible in 学. One proposal says it was added to 學 in Western Zhou forms to mark a child learner; its present-day function in 学 remains unresolved.

history.text: The selected early-style image is a modern vector tracing identified as an oracle-bone-style form of 學. It shows a detached mark above crossing strokes, an angular middle section, and a distinct lower shape with two descending strokes. Its appearance alone does not establish component identity or settle the competing construction analyses.
學 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 学. The graphic path from early forms to either modern shape is not established here.

A later lexicographic account describes 學 as an abbreviated seal-script form of 斆, which it analyzes as 教 and 冖 with 𦥑 supplying the sound. This received account does not confirm the structure of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The early construction accounts remain distinct. One interprets some forms as 𦥑 (two hands) with tally-like elements 五 and 六, while allowing that 爻 may supply a sound cue in some forms. Other proposals describe associative structures involving 升 + 冖 or 林 + 冖; phonosemantic structures with 爻 as sound and 升 or 冖 as the other element; and a separate unusual element read jù as both sound and meaning, depicted as hands or claws. These proposals do not establish one construction for every early form.
The graphic path from early 學 forms to 学 is unresolved. The modern top alone does not establish an ancient roof component or a specific corruption.
An oracle-bone occurrence is reported, but its archaeological date and context are not specified beyond that identification.

senses.text: Learning or study is a present-day meaning of 学. One source proposes learning and emulation—following something as a model—as early meanings of 學; this is an interpretation, not a settled original meaning. A reported oracle-bone occurrence does not by itself resolve the graph’s sense.

senses.period: current; school use attested for 學 in bronze inscriptions
senses.text: 學 is attested in bronze inscriptions for a school. In present-day compounds such as 小學、中學 and 大學, 学 is a morpheme naming an educational institution or place of learning; these examples do not establish 学 as a standalone word meaning “school.” The evidence does not establish when the school use began.
A bronze-inscription example concerns archery instruction. The evidence does not establish a full semantic sequence from learning to teaching.
The phrase 成學 is reported with the meaning “complete one’s studies”; it illustrates a contextual use of 學.

senses.gloss: feel; perceive, written with the graph 學
senses.text: In Han slips, 學 is reported as a borrowed spelling for the different word 覺, “feel” or “perceive.” The reason for this spelling is not established. This is a spelling loan, not a meaning that developed from “learning”.

developments.text: Learning and school uses are both reported, but the examples do not show that one developed from the other or establish their relative timing.
Learning and instruction are both documented, but their chronology and any specific semantic transition are not established.

limitations.text: Period-separated examples do not establish a complete chronology or every link among learning, school, instruction, imitation, and knowledge.
The reported Han use of 學 for 覺 has no earlier occurrence or complete sound history documented here.

overview.text: 学 means learning or study and is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學. Its upper assembly, ⺍ over 冖, sits above 子; these current parts do not settle the ancient construction.

components.text: ⺍ is the top subpart of 学’s upper assembly, with 冖 below it; the assembly’s function is unresolved.
冖 is the middle part of 学’s upper assembly; its shape alone does not establish a roof meaning or ancient role here.
